source_meta._title: Fall damage is ignored for a couple of seconds when reloading into LAN or singleplayer worlds

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition 1.4.2 in a disposable singleplayer world using the integrated server. Create the setup in Creative mode with cheats enabled, then enter Survival mode for the fall. Do not use a dedicated multiplayer server, because the report explicitly excludes vanilla dedicated-server worlds.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact Java Edition version Minecraft 1.4.2; do not use the listed fix version Minecraft 1.4.3.
Use a new or otherwise disposable singleplayer world so that dying or altering terrain cannot damage a valuable save.

Use default controls or their rebound equivalents: E for inventory, T for chat, Esc for the pause menu, Space for jump/ascend, W for forward movement, left-click for breaking, and right-click for placing blocks.
Enable cheats during world creation so that the player can switch from Creative mode to Survival mode.
Use a normal non-Hardcore world. No seed, dimension, or coordinates are required by the report.
Before the test fall, the player must have full health, no armor equipped, no status effects, and no fall-damage-reducing equipment.
The landing surface must be ordinary solid ground. It must not contain water, ladders, vines, cobwebs, beds, or other blocks that could interrupt or modify the fall.
The exact report command `/fill ~3 ~ ~ ~3 ~45 ~ minecraft:polished_andesite` is not executable in Minecraft 1.4.2. Build an equivalent 46-block-tall solid pillar manually as described below.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher profile configured for the exact version Minecraft 1.4.2, launch the game, and wait for the main menu.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft 1.4.2 main menu is visible.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, open More World Options, set Allow Cheats to ON, and create the world. Leave the seed unspecified and do not select Hardcore mode.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> More World Options... -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: A new singleplayer world has loaded and the player can fly and place blocks without consuming them.

steps.action: Wait until nearby terrain has rendered and player movement responds normally. Find a flat area of solid ground with at least a 7-by-7-block unobstructed landing zone and at least 50 blocks of open air above it.
steps.success_cue: A flat solid landing area and sufficient vertical clearance are available in loaded terrain.

steps.action: While still in Creative mode, clear plants, trees, overhangs, water, or other obstacles from the intended landing zone. Left-click unwanted blocks to remove them. Keep the center and surrounding ground solid and exposed to the sky.
steps.success_cue: The intended landing zone is ordinary solid ground with no block that could catch the player or alter fall damage.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Select Stone, or another ordinary full solid block available in Minecraft 1.4.2, and place it into one of the nine hotbar slots at the bottom of the inventory. Close the inventory and select that hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: An ordinary solid building block is selected in the active hotbar slot.

steps.action: At one edge of the cleared landing area, place one solid block on the ground as the pillar base. Double-tap Space to begin Creative flight. Ascend and place 45 additional blocks directly above the base, one at a time, producing a straight one-block-wide column containing 46 blocks from bottom to top. Aim at the top face of the highest block and right-click to add each next block.
steps.exact_input: double-tap Space; right-click once per block until 45 additional blocks have been placed
steps.success_cue: A straight 46-block-tall solid pillar stands beside the cleared landing zone, equivalent in height to the inclusive Y-to-Y+45 range in the report command.

steps.action: While flying, move above the pillar's top block. Carefully descend until directly over its top face, then double-tap Space to stop flying and settle onto the top block. Do not step off yet.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary on the top face of the pillar, approximately 45 blocks above the ground.

steps.action: Turn so that moving forward from the pillar will send the player toward the center of the cleared solid landing zone rather than toward another structure, water, or the pillar itself.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair faces open air above the cleared landing zone, with solid ground directly below the intended fall path.

steps.action: Press E and verify that all armor slots are empty. Do not equip Feather Falling boots or any other armor. Close the inventory.
steps.success_cue: All armor slots are empty and the player remains standing on the pillar.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Type the Minecraft 1.4.2-compatible game-mode command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds, the health and hunger HUD becomes visible, and the player is now in Survival mode.

steps.action: Confirm that the health bar is full, no status-effect indicator is present, and the player is still standing on top of the pillar. If health is not full or the player has an effect or armor, reset those conditions before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Survival-mode player has full health, no armor, no status effects, and a clear fall path to ordinary solid ground.

steps.action: Jump outward from the pillar toward the cleared landing zone by pressing Space while holding W briefly. Release movement input after clearing the top block so that no later input changes the test unnecessarily.
steps.success_cue: The player is airborne, descending toward the cleared solid ground, and is no longer above the pillar's top face.

steps.action: Watch the ground approach. While the player is still airborne but close enough that landing would occur almost immediately after resuming—approximately 3 to 6 blocks above the ground—press Esc once. Do not wait until the player has already contacted the ground.
steps.success_cue: The singleplayer pause menu appears while the saved player position is still airborne above the landing zone.

steps.action: On the pause menu, immediately click Save and Quit to Title. Do not choose Back to Game.
steps.success_cue: Saving finishes and the title screen appears; the test world is no longer running.

steps.action: From the title screen, click Singleplayer and select the same test world that was just saved. Do not create a new world or open a different save.
steps.success_cue: The same test world is highlighted in the singleplayer world list.

steps.action: Click Play Selected World, or double-click the selected world, to reload it. Do not open the world through a dedicated server.
steps.success_cue: The loading screen begins for the same world in which the player was saved while falling.

steps.action: As soon as the gameplay view returns, provide no movement, jump, or interaction input. End setup actions immediately so the observation subsystem can monitor the resumed fall and the player's health through the first ground contact.
steps.success_cue: The same world has loaded at the saved airborne position and the player is resuming the fall over the cleared solid landing area without additional input.

stor.handoff_condition: The same singleplayer world has just been reloaded from the save made while the Survival-mode player was airborne near the ground. No post-load movement or interaction input has been given, and the player is resuming the fall toward the cleared solid landing surface. Begin observing the health HUD immediately through the first ground contact.
uncertainties: The report's exact command `/fill ~3 ~ ~ ~3 ~45 ~ minecraft:polished_andesite` was written for a substantially newer command and block registry than the first listed affected version. External version-history verification indicates that `/fill` was added in 14w03a and andesite was added in 14w02a, so neither is available in Minecraft 1.4.2. The plan therefore preserves the commanded inclusive height of 46 blocks but constructs the pillar manually from an ordinary solid block.

The report gives no world seed, coordinates, difficulty, or tower surroundings. A disposable Creative-mode setup world, an unobstructed flat landing area, and ordinary solid ground are practical choices rather than report-mandated requirements.

The report applies to both singleplayer and LAN-hosted worlds but excludes vanilla dedicated-server worlds. This plan selects singleplayer because it is the simplest deterministic affected environment and because Esc pauses the integrated singleplayer world while the player is airborne.

The report only says to exit before hitting the ground and does not give an exact remaining height. Approximately 3 to 6 blocks above the ground is selected to make ground contact occur shortly after the world reloads; visual timing may require a retry if the player lands before Esc opens the pause menu.

The historical command `/gamemode 0` is used to enter Survival mode in Minecraft 1.4.2. If the installation unexpectedly rejects the command despite cheats being enabled, use the version's game-mode control to enter Survival without changing any other test condition.
